headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: ACI’s CRM/email outputs can feed AutoGPT’s shell/filesystem actions, creating default-path exfiltration and unsafe downstream execution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can ingest and emit CRM, email, Slack, Notion, and Google Sheets content, while AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses. If ACI forwards untrusted content into files or messages that AutoGPT consumes, instruction-like payloads can cross the pair. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not high.
conditions: IF ACI writes untrusted external content into a shared file or message queue that AutoGPT reads
IF AutoGPT parses file or workspace content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared workspace or message bridge between the agents
Require provenance tags on all ACI-generated content before AutoGPT reads it
Add a manual review step for any file AutoGPT consumes from ACI
Use separate directories and credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches email, CRM, customer support, calendar, and research data and has broad network egress; AutoGPT can access the filesystem and has allowlisted network egress. If ACI places sensitive records into files or prompts that AutoGPT then transmits or stores, leakage can occur in default workflows. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF ACI writes customer or email data into a shared filesystem readable by AutoGPT
IF AutoGPT sends its context or file contents to an allowlisted external endpoint
mitigations: Keep ACI and AutoGPT on separate workspaces
Block AutoGPT from reading ACI-managed files by default
Restrict ACI outputs to redacted summaries only
Audit outbound destinations on AutoGPT’s allowlist
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ACI supports multiple instances and broad API-driven operations, while AutoGPT does not support multiple instances and can write to the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. Overlap on mutable resources can create conflicts if both touch the same workspace or external service state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the conflict is plausible but not proven severe.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem directory
IF both agents mutate the same external API-backed resource without locks
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared resources
Disable concurrent runs of AutoGPT on the same workspace
Use a single orchestrator lock file
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM, email, calendar, and research outputs, and AutoGPT can act on files and shell commands. If AutoGPT treats ACI output as authoritative, a mistaken lead, email draft, or task plan can cascade into irreversible external actions. The pair’s default tool-rich setup makes this a realistic downstream execution risk.
conditions: IF AutoGPT consumes ACI output without verification
IF AutoGPT uses ACI-generated text to trigger shell commands, file writes, or external API actions
mitigations: Require human approval before AutoGPT acts on ACI output
Add a verification step that checks ACI outputs against source data
Limit AutoGPT to read-only handling of ACI artifacts
Log and diff all ACI-to-AutoGPT handoffs
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or personal data from ACI is stored or forwarded by AutoGPT under different retention or residency rules. No specific certifications are documented, so the safest choice is medium.
conditions: IF ACI data includes regulated personal data
IF AutoGPT stores or forwards that data under a different retention or residency policy
mitigations: Classify ACI data before handing it to AutoGPT
Redact personal data from shared artifacts
Set a short retention window for AutoGPT files
Restrict AutoGPT egress destinations
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents
